lead.kicker: TOP STORY  •  SAUDI ARABIA AND YEMEN
lead.headline: Yemen’s War Reaches Saudi Oil and Airports
lead.deck: A missile hit an Aramco building on Wednesday, and Riyadh’s airport is still shut.
body: Yemen is a country just south of Saudi Arabia. A group there called the Houthis is fighting Yemen’s government, which Saudi Arabia backs. On Wednesday, the Houthis said they struck an Aramco site in Dhahran. Aramco is Saudi Arabia’s giant oil company. A Saudi official said a building was hit, causing a small fire and no injuries.

On Thursday, Saudi-backed forces said they stopped a drone heading for the city of Medina and a missile fired toward the capital, Riyadh. Over the weekend, attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid airport reportedly killed 14 people and wounded more than 300. The airport is expected to stay shut until at least Saturday.

Ordinary families in Yemen are suffering too. The UN World Food Programme says the fighting is cutting food aid to about 800,000 people. In the city of Taiz, wheat flour is nearly gone. Meanwhile, a meeting between the European Union and Gulf countries in Riyadh has been postponed.

lead.why: Airports and oil sites matter far beyond Yemen, and the people hit hardest are families who cannot easily get food.

world.headline: Russia Hits Ukraine’s Power Again, and Kyiv Ends Its Pause
world.deck: More than half a million people lost electricity after the latest attacks.
body: Ukraine is in the fifth year of a war with Russia. On Sunday, US President Donald Trump announced an “energy ceasefire”, a pause in attacks on power plants and oil sites. It did not hold. Overnight into Wednesday, Russian attacks killed at least nine people and left more than half a million without electricity.

Russia said it hit two plants that supply power and heat in the capital, Kyiv, and another in Kharkiv. Ukraine, in turn, has been hitting Russian oil refineries. On Thursday, Russia said Ukraine struck a refinery in Ryazan, south of Moscow. Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said Kyiv was done with the pause.

Zelenskyy was due to meet European leaders in Brussels on Thursday. He wants tougher sanctions on Russia, which are penalties meant to hurt its economy. The EU has promised Ukraine $50 billion next year, but Ukraine plans to spend $175 billion on defence.

us.headline: US Prices Rose 3.7% in a Year, Led by Petrol
us.deck: It was the last inflation report before the November 3 elections.
body: Inflation is how fast prices rise. On Wednesday, the government’s Bureau of Labor Statistics said prices in September were 3.7% higher than a year earlier. In August the figure was 3.4%.
Petrol was the main cause. Petrol prices rose 9.1% in September alone, and they are 34.2% higher than a year ago. The AAA motoring group says regular petrol averages $4.33 a gallon and diesel $6.29.

Rising prices could lead the Federal Reserve, the US central bank, to raise interest rates again. In September it raised them for the first time in three years. A Reuters/Ipsos poll found about 78% of Americans blame President Trump’s policies for higher prices.
us.why: Petrol prices touch almost everything, because trucks and ships carry nearly everything we buy.

india.headline: Young Protesters Join the Voter-List Row
india.deck: Police detained about 20 volunteers at Jantar Mantar on Tuesday.
body: A voter list is the official list of people allowed to vote. India’s Election Commission has been revising these lists, and media reports say more than 133 million names were removed. Opposition parties say this helps the ruling BJP and hurts minorities. The Commission denies wrongdoing and says the aim was to remove duplicate, dead or fraudulent names.

On Monday, thousands marched toward the Supreme Court in New Delhi, calling on the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, to resign. On Tuesday, police detained about 20 volunteers of the Cockroach Janta Party, a youth movement, at Jantar Mantar. This is a famous protest spot in Delhi that police said on Monday was no longer an official protest site.

Indian media reported that Rahul Gandhi also filed a Supreme Court petition for opposition leaders against the Commission. Human Rights Watch urged India to stop “arbitrary” arrests of young protesters. The Commission says anyone wrongly deleted from the list can sign up again.
india.why: Voting is how citizens choose leaders, so a fair and accurate voter list is something people everywhere care about.

sports.title: FOOTBALL
sports.body: The Saudi Pro League moved three games because of missile threats. Al Ahli v Al Nassr, Cristiano Ronaldo’s team, is now set for 6 March 2027. Two other games move to 19 December. On Monday, Al Nassr’s Asian Champions League match in Riyadh started an hour late after a missile was stopped.
